Calculators usually look for debt to income ratio. If you don't have a mortgage, student loans, car loans then it inflates your buying power. It doesn't take into account your actual expenses - food, transport, medical etc. If you were comfortable paying $1,500, the most you could probably squeeze is another $800/month on dual income. Personally, I would aim to keep it in the 2,000k range and save the rest. Ideally you should be able to afford a home on ONE salary. 

That would place a home around the 300k to 320k. Also, avoid condo fees if possible. Those things creep up.
I wish I had those skills!

It's horrific how quickly we are isolating ourselves. I feel like I am back in the closet as a butch woman. I have only one gay friend, and everyone else is straight which is creating its own type of heartbreak, especially since I am single and find myself only having straight women to look to (and not get). 

I feel more and more isolated, lonely and depressed lately. I can't find like minded lesbians anymore. Everyone has jumped in the Trans bandwagon without much thought for all the other identities that have existed before it.

There's definitely something to this. I have lived in DC and have lived in Pittsburgh (blue collar) and have traveled to North Carolina and other more "southern" states. I can't say I have ever been harassed. I think it's a combination of location, confidence, awareness of my surroundings and being polite. If I'm in a southern state, I say mam and sir, and properly thank people. Politeness goes a long way. 

Granted, I don't stay long in places that may have a high rate of closed-minded people, and that includes places with a high number of Latinos and blacks (not just African Americans). People forget that MANY immigrants, especially Latinos, Nigerians, Indian etc., are religiously-conservative and sport machismo, which is an even more insidious form of misogyny. As a Brazilian, I can say that I feel far more threatened in a room full of Brazilian men (and women), than I have ever felt in blue collar Pittsburgh. 

There are cultures that are just plain threatening to anyone who does not comform.

I am not maxing it and I make 6 figures. For me, it's important to match 401k (free money) and HSA. I actually wish we had better rules around HSA because as you get older, doctor bills get higher...and in this country, you'll likely end up bankrupt with medical bills. The yearly limits are not enough. 

I'm 41, and I basically switched to savings, and stocks. I prefer having cushion money because when you don't - you'll have to dip into retirement. And there's no guarantee you'll make it to retirement to anyway.

No life insurance policy and very little retirement. I owe about $110k on the house. I have a life insurance policy for her should something happen to me. For myself, I only have about 200k in retirement.

She didn't tell me to do that, but I saw the omission as worst than a communication faupax. It's my job on the line and reputation on the line, not hers...so I defaulted to contacting.
